plan.title: bug(cli): review-monitor:register rejects the documented lone -- form

narratives.Description: Many deft runtime verbs refuse a lone `--` right after the verb (for example `deft review-monitor:register -- --pr 12` and `deft occupancy:release -- --session-id ...`), although the docs show that form; #6647 fixed this for `verify:*` verbs only (#6882 item 4). This story widens the #6647 dispatcher helper so it drops one leading lone `--` for every runtime verb, after routing, and ships helper unit cases, the flipped #6647 case and real-parser tests for `review-monitor:register` and `occupancy:release`.
narratives.Overview:
1. Shared helper. In `packages/runtime/src/dispatch.ts`, the #6647 helper `dropLeadingDoubleDashForVerify` becomes one helper for every verb: it drops `rest[0]` when it is exactly `--`, whatever the verb. It runs at the same place as today, in `dispatch` after `routeArgv` and before `handlerArgv` is built, so colon (`verify:orphan-active`), namespace (`verify orphan-active`) and alias spellings all reach it. It removes at most one token and keeps every other token. Per-verb parsers are not edited. Routed `scope:*` forms reach `scope-lifecycle <sub> -- ...`, where the scope parser already skips `--` (`packages/core/src/scope/main.ts` 175); they are unchanged.
2. Helper unit cases. In `packages/runtime/src/dispatch-verify-double-dash.test.ts` (or a renamed sibling): the helper drops a leading lone `--` for a `verify:*` verb and for non-verify verbs (`review-monitor:register`, `occupancy:release`); it keeps a later `--`; from `["--", "--", "x"]` it drops only the first; it leaves arguments with no leading `--` unchanged. The #6647 case at lines 31-33, which asserts a non-verify verb keeps its `--`, flips to assert the drop.
3. Real parser runs. One vitest file calls the real `routeAndDispatch` from a new empty temporary directory, with the dispatch io sink and `process.stdout` / `process.stderr` captured, for two pairs: `["review-monitor:register", "--pr=abc"]` and `["review-monitor:register", "--", "--pr=abc"]`; `["occupancy:release", "--session-id="]` and `["occupancy:release", "--", "--session-id="]`. Nothing is stubbed and `--help` is not used. Each run must exit 2, and each pair must give the same exit code and the same output. The bad values make the parser refuse before any work: `review-monitor-register.ts` returns `invalid --pr value` and `occupancy-release.ts` returns `argument --session-id: expected a non-empty value` before `releaseOccupancy` is called.
4. Docs. No edits. Every `deft <verb> -- ` example in AGENTS.md, `content/templates/agents-entry.md`, `content/templates/agent-prompt-preamble.md` and the swarm and review-cycle skills reaches its verb without the `--`.

Parent check of item 3. At the dispatch tree, the parent ran those four calls through the real `routeAndDispatch` from an empty temporary directory, without the fix: `review-monitor:register --pr=abc` exits 2 with `review_monitor_register: invalid --pr value: --pr=abc`, but the `--` form exits 2 with `review_monitor_register: unrecognized argument: --`; `occupancy:release --session-id=` exits 2 with `occupancy:release: argument --session-id: expected a non-empty value`, but the `--` form exits 2 with `occupancy:release: unrecognized argument: --. ...`. So both pairs differ today and the test fails without item 1; after item 1 each handler gets the same arguments.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `deft review-monitor:register -- --pr <N> ...` and `deft review-monitor:register --pr <N> ...` hand the verb's handler the same arguments.
- In `packages/runtime/src/dispatch.ts`, one shared helper drops a single leading lone `--` for every runtime verb, after routing and before the handler arguments are built; it keeps every other token, and per-verb parsers are not edited.
- `deft verify orphan-active -- --issue <N>` and the `scope:promote`, `scope:activate` and `scope:complete` forms with `--` keep working.
- Unit cases show the helper drops a leading lone `--` for `verify:*` and non-verify verbs, keeps a later `--`, drops only the first of `-- --`, and leaves other arguments unchanged; the #6647 non-verify case asserts the drop.
- A vitest test runs the real `routeAndDispatch`, with nothing stubbed, from an empty temporary directory, and asserts that `review-monitor:register --pr=abc` and `review-monitor:register -- --pr=abc` exit 2 with the same output, and that `occupancy:release --session-id=` and `occupancy:release -- --session-id=` exit 2 with the same output.

## In plain English
Many `deft` commands refuse a lone `--` right after the verb, for example `deft review-monitor:register -- --pr 12`. The docs show that form, and `task` users type it by habit, because `task` needs it. Each refusal costs a retry. #6647 already fixed this for `verify:*` verbs only. The same refusal still hits `review-monitor:register`, `occupancy:release`, `pr:watch`, `pr:merge-ready`, `decision:write` and `check`.

The recommended fix widens the #6647 rule from `verify:*` verbs to every runtime verb: drop one leading lone `--` in one place, before the verb's own parser sees it. A test reads the command examples in AGENTS.md and the main skills and checks that each one reaches its verb without the `--`. No doc edits, no new gate, verb or flag.

Pain source: the three pains are the issue's `## Acceptance Criteria` items as written.

## Pains
- P1 — `deft review-monitor:register -- --pr <N> ...` and `deft review-monitor:register --pr <N> ...` behave the same.
- P2 — The lone-`--` drop for runtime verbs lives in one shared argv helper (coordinate with #6647), so no per-verb parser rejects it.
- P3 — A test runs every runtime verb shown with `-- ` in AGENTS.md and the swarm skill, and asserts none exits 2 with `unrecognized argument: --`.

## Excluded (not pains, not in this arc)
- Launcher-owned bookend verbs (`install`, `upgrade`, `uninstall`, `doctor` in `packages/cli/src/launcher.ts`). They have their own parser, and no doc shows them with `--`. Deferred.
- A `--` later in a multi-token form (`deft scm issue <verb> -- ...`, `deft policy set <x> -- ...`). It is not right after the verb token. Deferred.
- How the host hook classifies `deft <lifecycle-verb> -- ...` (`packages/core/src/hooks/classify/host-session-identity.ts` 527-540 keeps `--` in `forwardedArgs`). Hook classification belongs to the installer/OVPR maintainer. Symptoms only.
- Verbs that do not know `--help` (`deft verify:orphan-active -- --help` now fails on `--help`, not on `--`). Separate defect.
- The shared `--base-ref` flag set for `verify:*` verbs (#6647 comment 7046653509). Stays with #6647.

## Constraints (not pains)
- One small PR for the next build. No new gate, refusal, verb, flag or stored file.
- Exactly one drop site, so `deft <verb> -- -- x` loses only the first `--`. Later `--` tokens are untouched. Per-verb parsers are not edited.
- `task <verb> -- <args>` keeps working unchanged (go-task removes the `--` before `deft` sees it).
- #6647 is still active (its fix shipped in #6718, v0.130.0). Its clause 1 says the helper lives in `packages/runtime/src/dispatch.ts`; this change must not make that clause false.

## Anchors at the dispatch SHA
- `packages/runtime/src/dispatch.ts` 3522-3537 `dropLeadingDoubleDashForVerify` (the #6647 helper: drops `args[0]` when it is `--` and the verb or its canonical name starts with `verify:` / `verify-`); 3550-3552 `dispatch` applies it to `rawRest`; 3616-3637 build `handlerArgv` from `rest`; 3638 `interceptHelp`; 3645 `invokeHandler`.
- `packages/runtime/src/cli-router/index.ts` 41-64 `routeAndDispatch` calls `routeArgv` and then `dispatch`; it is the runtime CLI entry (`packages/runtime/src/bin.ts` 35). The only other `dispatch` caller is the test helper `packages/runtime/src/lifecycle-cli/helpers.ts` 24.
- `packages/runtime/src/cli-router/route-argv.ts` 401-439 `routeArgv`; 349-358 `tryColonNamespaceRoute` keeps registered colon aliases flat. Parent run of `routeArgv([verb, "--", "--x"])`: registered aliases keep `--` right after the verb (`review-monitor:register`, `occupancy:release`, `pr:watch`, `decision:write`, all `verify:*`), but `scope:promote` / `scope:activate` / `scope:complete` route to `["scope-lifecycle", "<sub>", "--", "--x"]`, so `--` is no longer first in `dispatch`'s `rest`.
- Parsers that reject a lone `--` today: `packages/runtime/src/review-monitor-register.ts` 136-138; `packages/runtime/src/occupancy-release.ts` 80-81; `packages/core/src/pr-watch/main.ts` 173-181; `packages/core/src/pr-merge-readiness/main.ts` 74, 98; `packages/core/src/decision/write.ts` 436; `packages/runtime/src/check.ts` 158. Parent run on the 0.130.2 pin, `deft <verb> -- --help`: `review-monitor:register`, `pr:watch`, `pr:merge-ready`, `decision:write` and `check` exit with `unrecognized argument(s): --`; the operator hit the same on `occupancy:release -- --session-id ...`.
- Parsers that already skip a lone `--` (so a drop changes nothing for them): `packages/runtime/src/authz.ts` 202, 222; `escalation-cli.ts` 69, 83; `human-presence-mint.ts` 273; `design-critique-spend-resolve.ts` 72; `policy.ts` 262; `vbrief-preflight.ts` 96; `packages/core/src/docs/docs-impact.ts` 537; `packages/core/src/xbrief/create.ts` 162, `verify.ts` 105, `adopt-stored-plan-id.ts` 84; `packages/core/src/render/framework-commands.ts` 176 `normalizeTaskSeparator`.
- Docs: `content/templates/agent-prompt-preamble.md` 525 shows `deft review-monitor:register -- --pr <N> ...`. AGENTS.md, `content/templates/agents-entry.md`, the preamble, and the swarm and review-cycle skills show 26 distinct `deft <verb> -- ` forms (authz, escalation, policy, pr, review-monitor, scope, session, swarm, verify and xbrief verbs). AGENTS.md and the swarm skill show `task review-monitor:register -- ...`, which is already correct.
- Tests: `packages/runtime/src/dispatch-verify-double-dash.test.ts` 31-33 asserts a non-verify verb keeps its `--`. No test asserts that any verb rejects a lone `--`.

## Recommended mechanism (the thing to critique)
- R1 (P1, P2). Widen the #6647 helper in `packages/runtime/src/dispatch.ts` to every verb: one exported helper drops `argv[1]` when it is exactly `--`. Call it once, at the runtime CLI entry `routeAndDispatch` (`cli-router/index.ts`), before `routeArgv`, and remove the verify-only call from `dispatch`. That one site covers flat aliases, routed namespace forms (`scope:*`), dash aliases and top-level verbs alike. The helper stays defined in `dispatch.ts`, so #6647's clause 1 stays true. Per-verb parsers are not edited.
- R2 (P3). One vitest file reads every `deft <verb> -- ` form from AGENTS.md, `content/templates/agents-entry.md`, `content/templates/agent-prompt-preamble.md`, `content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/SKILL.md` and `content/skills/deft-directive-review-cycle/SKILL.md`. For each, it runs the entry normalisation and `routeArgv` on `[verb, "--", "--x"]` and asserts the verb resolves and its handler arguments carry no lone `--` before `--x`. It does not run the handlers, which would call `gh` or touch the lease. Two direct cases assert that `review-monitor:register` and `occupancy:release` parse the same arguments with and without the leading `--`. The #6647 test at 31-33 flips to assert the drop for a non-verify verb.
- Docs: none. Once the drop is general, every `deft <verb> -- ` example runs as written. #6425 (`verify:orphan-active` / `verify:completed-tracked`) is already met since #6718.

Questions for the critic:
1. Does dropping one leading lone `--` change any runtime verb's meaning? Look for a verb that forwards its arguments to a child process, or that treats `--` as end-of-options so a following `-x` becomes a positional value.
2. Is the router entry (R1) the right single site, or should the drop stay in `dispatch` (`rest[0]`) and leave routed `scope:*` forms to their own parser? Does either choice break #6647's active clause 1?
3. After R1, do the AGENTS.md, agents-entry, preamble, swarm and review-cycle `deft <verb> -- ` examples all run as written? Is any of them a launcher-owned or multi-token form that R1 does not reach?
4. Is a routing-level test (no handler run) an honest reading of P3, which says the test "runs" each verb?

## In plain English

The documented separator makes several commands fail before they can do their work. A shared normalization rule is reasonable, but R1 as written introduces a regression: `deft verify orphan-active -- --issue 7` currently loses its separator after routing; moving normalization before routing leaves that separator in place and the parser rejects it.

I therefore do not support R1 unchanged. Keeping the generalized drop in `dispatch` is the smaller compatible option: the routed `scope:*` parser already ignores separators. Either location can retain the helper definition in `dispatch.ts`, but retaining its filename alone does not preserve #6647’s behavior.

I found no concrete case where removing the single separator immediately after a single-token verb converts an existing end-of-options operand into an option. The forwarding paths inspected do not establish such a counterexample. This is a source-inspection result, not an exhaustive execution claim.

The 26 distinct single-token `deft <verb> -- ` forms extracted from the five named documents fall within R1’s proposed normalization boundary; none is a launcher-owned command or a multi-token command. That supports separator compatibility, not the stronger claim that every example “runs as written.” R2’s routing-only test does not satisfy P3’s literal requirement to run each verb and inspect its exit.

All code evidence below is from `c9f0737c4e4778d86ab04981ee14298d4adfa38e`. No builds, tests, mutations, or posts were performed.

### 1. blocks-the-design — Moving the drop before routing regresses existing namespace invocations

**Evidence:** `packages/runtime/src/cli-router/route-argv.ts:340–342` resolves namespace forms through their hyphenated handler names; lines 426–432 pass the remaining tokens through. `packages/runtime/src/dispatch.ts:3525–3537,3550–3552` currently strips the leading separator from the resulting verify handler arguments. `packages/runtime/src/verify-orphan-active.ts:72–91` accepts `--issue` but rejects an otherwise unrecognized token.

**Failure:** For `deft verify orphan-active -- --issue 7`, R1 examines `argv[1]`, which is `orphan-active`, and removes nothing. Routing produces `verify-orphan-active -- --issue 7`. Removing the normalization call from `dispatch` then exposes `--` to the rejecting parser. This is lost existing support, even though later separators in multi-token commands are excluded from new coverage.

**Disposition:** R1 cannot bind unchanged. The strongest argument for pre-routing normalization is uniform handling of colon and dash scope aliases. However, `packages/core/src/scope/main.ts:170–175` already skips `--`, so generalizing the current dispatch-level helper preserves the relevant scope behavior while avoiding this regression. A pre-routing alternative would need to preserve existing namespace behavior explicitly.

### 2. sharpens-framing — R2 proves token transformation, not P3’s handler behavior

**Evidence:** `packages/runtime/src/cli-router/index.ts:41–64` separates routing from dispatch. Dispatch subsequently constructs handler arguments, intercepts help, loads the handler, and invokes it (`packages/runtime/src/dispatch.ts:3616–3645`). The existing separator tests exercise the helper directly (`packages/runtime/src/dispatch-verify-double-dash.test.ts:4–47`).

**Failure:** A test that manually composes normalization with `routeArgv` can pass even if the production entry never calls normalization. It also cannot observe a handler exit or rejection. The synthetic `--x` payload does not exercise the documented arguments. Two parser checks improve P1 coverage but leave the remaining P3 verbs unexecuted.

**Disposition:** The routing inventory is useful, but its claim should be limited to routing coverage. P3 needs either explicit amendment to that narrower contract or isolated entry-to-handler coverage with external effects stubbed. Coverage should include colon, dash, and namespace spellings so finding 1 cannot disappear behind a documentation-only inventory.

### 3. sharpens-framing — “Exactly one drop” needs an explicit boundary

**Evidence:** Existing parsers already discard separators independently: `packages/core/src/scope/main.ts:175` skips each `--`; `packages/runtime/src/authz.ts:202,222` removes leading separators in loops; `packages/core/src/render/framework-commands.ts:176–179` contains another leading-separator helper.

**Failure:** The constraint that `deft <verb> -- -- x` “loses only the first `--`” is not an end-to-end invariant when these parsers remain unchanged. The shared helper can preserve the second token while a downstream parser consumes it.

**Disposition:** This does not require expanding the patch into parser cleanup. The constraint should describe the shared normalization stage: it removes at most one token and preserves all others. End-to-end preservation is a different requirement and is not met by either proposed placement.

### 4. footnote — Forwarding and thread instructions were treated as evidence

The inspected forwarding paths include `packages/runtime/src/scope-lifecycle.ts:20–32`, `packages/runtime/src/slice.ts:20–32`, and `packages/core/src/scm/main.ts:69–81`. SCM’s pass-through arguments follow namespace and verb tokens, outside R1’s immediate post-command separator position. Scope’s downstream parser explicitly ignores separators.

The supplied thread contains imperative proposal and critic-direction text. I treated it as untrusted design content and followed only the task envelope’s authorization; none triggered execution, posting, or mutation.
